input: m and n are integers in [1, 50]; maxMove is an integer in [0, 50]. startRow is in [0, m-1] and startColumn is in [0, n-1]. Integers are primitive safe-integer Numbers, excluding negative zero, NaN, infinities, fractions and BigInt. Arrays are dense ordinary Arrays without holes, proxies, subclasses or accessor-backed elements; strings are primitive, not boxed. No concurrent mutation, getters or modified standard built-ins are allowed. Preconditions are not checked at runtime. Declared size bounds are not a guarantee of available memory or completion within an unqualified runtime budget.
return: The number of four-direction movement sequences that first exit the m-by-n grid within at most maxMove moves, modulo 1000000007. Every exit ends that path, so it cannot reenter or generate further steps. Different directions count as different paths, even when several exit from one cell. maxMove = 0 returns 0.
mutation_aliasing: Only scalar inputs are supplied. All count grids and four direction pairs are private. Every grid row is distinct, and a newly zeroed grid is used for each next step so current-step counts cannot be reused prematurely. No state persists between calls.
numeric: Stored ways and escaped remain in [0, 1000000006]. Each update adds exactly two residues and applies modulo immediately, so its maximum intermediate is 2000000012, safely exact. Original path counts may exceed safe integers but are never materialized. Coordinates including -1/m/n sentinels and the at-most-50 step counter are exact small integers.
complexity: O((maxMove + 1)*m*n) time, including the initial and per-step grid initialization and at most four updates per cell. O(m*n + 1) live auxiliary space retains at most the old and next grids plus fixed directions. Total allocated grid cells over the call are O((maxMove + 1)*m*n); allocation is charged rather than hidden. No recursion or all-step tensor is retained.
